verdicts.claim: The reconciliation tolerance formula and the worked example that defines its intent disagree by 13x, so the domain's only hard oracle has two incompatible definitions of "close enough".
verdicts.reason: Quotes verified verbatim. 10.02.02:47 states `tolerance = 0.5 × 10^-q + n × 0.5 × 10^-p`; :50 evaluates the 12-line p=q=2 case to £0.005 when the formula gives 0.065; :51's 400,000-line case (£0.205) matches the formula exactly, so the formula is the intended rule and :50 is the outlier. A second, independent contradiction sits in the same file and the auditor missed it: :53 says a fixed penny is 'too tight for the second and far too loose for the first' (tight for the DSR, loose for PRS) while D-10 at :199 states the exact reverse — 'too tight for a 12-line PRS statement and far too loose for a 400,000-line DSR'. D-10's direction agrees with the literal formula (£0.065 > £0.01); :50 and :53 agree with each other against it. So the file genuinely holds two incompatible accounts of the tolerance's direction on the small-statement case, and 'a penny out is a real failure' (:50) is false under the formula it illustrates. Downgraded from blocking because the normative artefact is unambiguous and stated twice (the code block at :47 and D-10 at :199); an implementer codes the formula and proceeds. The defect is that the prose defining its intent, and the worked example, are wrong — which misstates the behaviour of the domain's only hard oracle rather than blocking its construction.

verdicts.claim: The `Overdue` state routes the union of two causes of silence to 10.05.03 as a leakage finding, while the same file states that only one of those causes is leakage and that the platform cannot tell them apart.
verdicts.reason: All quotes verified. 10.02.01:258 makes Overdue's trigger 'calendared cycle passed, nothing arrived, and the cross-user signal says the source distributed' and routes it to 10.05.03 as a money-denominated finding; :195 repeats it; :114 states the cross-user signal separates only 'the first from the other two', i.e. it excludes cause (a) and leaves {(b),(c)}; the causes table at :111-112 marks (b) leakage and (c) 'No. A nag'; DT-09 at :279 concedes 'the platform cannot distinguish (b) from (c) alone'; and the cross-cut note at :296 states that feeding all three through 'would poison the domain's highest-confidence detector'. Checked for a resolution downstream and found none: 10.05.03 is [PARTIAL] (:5), its detector table (:31) takes '10.09 calendar + 10.02.01 cadence' as one expectation source with no notified/nag discrimination, and its only relevant guard is generic ('conservatism matters more than coverage', :54; D-02 :96 money only where knowable). Q-06 (:350) covers quorum numbers only. Partially mitigated and not fully: D-13's `notified` state (:255) removes cause (c) for sources whose notification is forwarded, so Overdue approximates (b) only where forwarding is configured — and (c) is called 'the modal case' (:112). Downgraded from blocking because the States table is a complete, buildable specification and DT-09 prescribes the honest posture ('a limit … it should be stated rather than discovered'), so an implementer proceeds; what is unresolved is what the finding claims about a population the file itself says is mostly not leakage.

verdicts.claim: The MoSCoW reasoning asserts the Must set is "exactly" D-03's ungated half, but four of the five things D-03 names as ungated are placed outside Must by the same table.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED. The quotes are accurate — royalties-collections-index.md:139 says 'exactly D-03's ungated half', D-03 at :112 names 10.02, 10.03, 10.05.01, 10.05.03 and 10.09, and the Must row at :134 omits 10.03.03, 10.03.04, 10.05.03 and 10.09 — but no reading diverges. The enumerated table (:134-137) is the scope statement, the section is headed 'MoSCoW Proposal' and labelled at :129 'Proposal only — the owner decides', and the same reasoning paragraph self-corrects two lines later: :141 'is Should not for its own value but because 10.05.03 cannot detect a missing distribution without it'. The ratified authority is moscow-ledger.md (:3-4, 'Owner decision (D-20)'), which this domain's own leaves cite as governing (10.01.02:53 cites 'moscow-ledger.md § WONT (53)'), and it agrees with the index table on all four disputed leaves (10.03.03 :308, 10.03.04 :309, 10.05.03 :311, 10.09 :313 all under '## SHOULD (285)' at :217). Nobody derives launch scope from an adjective when an enumerated, ratified table sits beside it. Prose overstatement, not ambiguity.

verdicts.claim: The domain sells a quantified onboarding moment that the feature which must produce it explicitly forbids, on data the same feature says usually does not exist.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the conflict is not unmarked; the owning feature quotes the exact phrase and adjudicates it three separate times. 10.05.01 DT-02 (:185) opens 'This is the acquisition hook … because "we found you £800" is the strongest message the platform has | The parent domain's Overview says exactly this, and it is right about the message' and rejects it as a strategy; DT-11 (:194) names 'the "we found you £800" framing' as its source and rejects it as a mechanism; DT-10 (:193) takes up precisely the amount question, rejects bare refusal as insufficient, and derives D-12 (:230) — the count and the not-knowing in one breath, with the copy spelled out at :144. 10.05-recovery-leakage-index.md D-04 (:47) and the CX files (royalties-collections-cx.md:103, 10.05-recovery-leakage-cx.md:53) all cite '£800' as the activation *framing* while D-03/D-12 govern what the screen says. The index sentence at :13 is a claim about the power of the moment ('the most powerful onboarding moment available'), not UI copy, and it is bounded in the same sentence ('it is a once-event, not a daily habit, which is why it is the activation and not the wedge'). An implementer building the activation surface reads 10.05.01, which forbids the figure explicitly.

verdicts.claim: 10.05.01's standing-search notification is required to be money-denominated and simultaneously forbidden from stating an amount.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED on a misread of the cited sibling decision. 10.05.01:108 and :178 both attribute the discipline to '10.05.03 D-03' — and 10.05.03 D-03 (:97) is 'One finding at a time, ranked, remediable', not a denomination rule. The denomination rule is the row above it: 10.05.03 D-02 (:96) 'Money is stated only where it is honestly knowable', with the matching state at :68 'Unsizable | Gap real, money unknown | Named without a number' and the constraint restated at :38 ('the platform mostly cannot say how much money is leaking'). That harmonises exactly with 10.05.01 D-03 (:221) and D-12 (:230): denominate where the pool published a sum, and say the amount is unknown — with the reason — where it did not (:144). royalties-collections-cx.md:319's loose citation of D-03 for 'money-denominated framing' is a citation slip, not a second rule; the file it points at answers the amount question in the adjacent row. No implementer is forced to choose between an invented figure and a muted notification.

verdicts.claim: 10.03.01 D-14 routes split-shortfall residuals into 10.02.05, whose reason taxonomy is declared closed and contains no code for them, and whose unit of record is the source identity rather than a fraction of an attributed line.
verdicts.reason: UPHELD. Every quote verified: 10.03.01 D-14 (:254) and the elaboration at :90 route the Σ<whole shortfall to 10.02.05 'where it is denominated, aged and alarmed'; this is a locked decision, not an open item — 10.03.01 Q-03 is struck through and marked '✅ Resolved this pass — DT-11, D-14'. On the receiving side 10.02.05:58 declares 'The set is closed: a line that fits none of these is a defect, not a new category', and none of the eleven codes at :62-72 fits: the nearest, `no-owner-as-of` (:67), is defined as '09 holds no split as-of that period', whereas the D-14 case has a split that sums to 97%. 10.02.05 has no record of the input anywhere — its Overview inputs (:11) list only matching, period and identifier failures; D-08 (:306) fixes the unit as the source identity 10.02.03 collapsed onto; and grepping the file for the shortfall finds nothing (its own word 'residual' at :105/:190/:302/:317 means the value-ranking tail, a different concept sharing the term). The queue's scope statement at :36 ('all money not attributed to a person') admits the residual in principle, which is why this is a warning rather than a contradiction — but the enumeration the spec itself declares closed and load-bearing has no cell for it, so an implementer either adds a twelfth code the spec calls a defect or files it under a code whose stated route cannot resolve it.

verdicts.claim: 10.02.05 Q-04 is a live open question whose stated premise its sibling has already falsified, and which that sibling records as resolved.
verdicts.reason: UPHELD. 10.02.05:326 still carries Q-04 as open (Owner: Agent, Deferred To: /create-prd-architecture) asserting 'Neither is stated in 10.02.01 today', and :78 repeats 'it requires a registry field that 10.02.01 does not currently state: Q-04'. Both statements are false against the sibling on disk: 10.02.01:41 opens the field table with 'Resolving 10.02.05 Q-04 — the registry owes two fields it did not previously state'; the Remittee row (:47) says '**Required by 10.02.05 D-15**'; the Correction window row (:51) says '**Required by 10.02.05 D-17**'; D-06 (:322) 'resolves 10.02.05 Q-04a'; D-16 (:332) 'Resolves 10.02.05 Q-04b'; and the cross-cut note (:292) states '`Q-04` there is resolved here (D-06, D-16)'. One-directional cross-reference rot: the resolving feature recorded the resolution, the asking feature was never updated. Forces no product invention (the auditor concedes this) but leaves a false statement about a sibling's data model inside a live question aimed at /create-prd-architecture.

verdicts.claim: Three product decisions in this unit are parked against a pipeline stage that has already completed, with no owner — a marker class the tree elsewhere recognises as expired and requiring promotion.
verdicts.reason: UPHELD, after testing the tracked-deferral defence and finding it fails. The markers exist as quoted: 10.04.03:62 'Platform shuts down … `[PENDING — Step 5]`'; 10.04.04:49 'Held money earns interest … `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`'; 10.04.04:53 'Platform is the disputant … `[PENDING — Step 5]` — who adjudicates against the house?'. The target stage is closed: ideation-index.md D-24 (:210) states '**Step 5 is now fully complete**: 195 Must=[DEEP], 285 Should=[PARTIAL]' and that 'Coulds (201) and Won'ts (53) correctly remain [SURFACE] — out of Step 5 scope'. Both files are [SURFACE] (10.04.03:5, 10.04.04:5) and both sit in moscow-ledger.md '## COULD (201)' (:577, :578), so they were out of scope and the stage will not return to them. A full grep of the domain confirms these three are the only expired markers — every other inline marker names a live stage (/write-be-spec, /create-prd-architecture). The tree's own remedy for this class is documented at 10.01.05:95 ('Promoted from Edge Cases, where it had expired against /ideate-discover Step 5'), and none of the three was promoted: 10.04.03's questions (Q-01 unpayable balances, Q-02 custody, Q-03 resolved) and 10.04.04's do not carry them, so all three sit with no owner and no stage.

verdicts.claim: 10.04.03 D-04 records threshold ownership as an aspiration ("ideally the payee's to set") that contradicts the unit's own Role Matrix and CX, and nothing tracks the choice.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED on convergence. The quotes hold — D-04 (:99) 'The **threshold is visible and justified**; ideally the payee's to set', the Role Matrix (10.04-disbursement-payee-statements-index.md:35) giving Musician read-only and Producer config, the CX 'sharp' asymmetry (10.04-disbursement-payee-statements-cx.md:63), and neither Q-01 nor Q-02 (:107-108) covering it — but the decision's own typography separates what is decided from what is wished: the bolded commitment is 'visible and justified', and 'ideally' is flagged as unrealised in its source hypothesis, DT-03 (:81), which ends '…and **ideally the payee's to set** — the last of which nobody in the industry does'. The access contract is stated twice against it and once inside the same file — the feature's own Role Lens (:19 Musician read-only, :20 Producer config) matches the index Role Matrix exactly. No competent implementer grants payees write access to a threshold on the strength of a hedged clause when the file's own Role Lens two dozen lines earlier says read-only. Unrealised aspiration recorded beside a decision, not a forced choice.

verdicts.claim: The overdue leakage finding is emitted by two features under different trigger rules, and 10.09's model lacks the calendared/triggered distinction its consumer requires — observed in a cross-cut note and tracked nowhere.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the consumer composes the two into one detector. 10.05.03:31 lists a single row, 'Distribution overdue | 10.09 calendar + 10.02.01 cadence | Statement arrivals': 10.09 supplies the date, 10.02.01 supplies the arrival observation and D-14's quorum, one detector consumes both. That is exactly what 10.02.01 D-09 (:325) locks — 'The registry reads 10.09's calendar and stores none of its own' — so there are not two copies of the expectation and not two emitters; 10.09's Overdue row (:66) describes the outcome from the calendar's side. The failure scenario also does not follow from 10.09's own model: its in-flight trigger is 'Registered, usage period closed' (:63, society registration), a distributor like DistroKid has no calendar, and :67 already routes that case — 'Unknown | No calendar for that body | The platform says it does not know, rather than guessing' — so no clock runs on a triggered source. What survives is narrow and disclosed: 10.02.01:295 records that 10.09 'does not currently make' the calendared/triggered distinction explicit, in a file whose D-08 (:324) owns the rule; 10.09 is [PARTIAL] at Should (:5), i.e. Level-1 depth with further deepening 'when reached' (ideation-index.md:171). A naming gap in a not-yet-deepened Should node, with the governing rule locked upstream.

verdicts.claim: The domain's MoSCoW places 10.01.01 at Should while the ratified global ledger places it at Could, unmarked on either side — and the Should-tier feature that hard-depends on it would then depend on a Could.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED. The divergence is real and correctly isolated (royalties-collections-index.md:135 Should; moscow-ledger.md:573 under '## COULD (201)' at :507; all 27 other domain-10 leaves agree), but the two documents declare their own relationship: the index section is headed 'MoSCoW Proposal' and marked at :129 'Proposal only — the owner decides', while the ledger is the ratified artefact ('Owner decision (D-20)', :4) that this domain's leaves cite as authority (10.01.02:53). Disk corroborates the ledger, not the proposal: 10.01.01 is [SURFACE] (:5), which ideation-index.md:67 defines as the Could/Won't state, whereas Should would require [PARTIAL]. The dependency inversion is also reasoned in the ledger rather than overlooked — :573 places 10.01.01 at Could explicitly 'for its main consumer 10.01.02', and :305 justifies 10.01.02 at Should as the ungated registration-readiness product ('even with no delivery relationship'), which reports a missing IPI as the gap rather than requiring one to be stored; per D-10 that missing identifier is the product's headline output. Tier is not sequence in any case: the ledger defers sequencing to /plan-phase (:4).

verdicts.claim: The domain index's structural claims about its own children no longer match the tree: it states all children are [SURFACE] and that 81 hypotheses are logged, while five children are [DEEP] and the tree carries roughly 163.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED. The arithmetic checks out — royalties-collections-index.md:28 ends 'All `[SURFACE]`', and per-file DT counts on disk are 17/13/13/10/15 for 10.02, 13/13/3/3 for 10.03 and 12/3/3 for 10.05 against the table's 15/12/9 — but the stale text is inside a date-stamped record of a past pass ('Classified 2026-07-16 through the Node Classification Gate', :26) whose figures describe that pass's output, and the authoritative depth cells sit two lines below it and are current (:33 shows `[DEEP]` for 10.02, matching disk). Depth is tracked by status, not by the Deep Think column: ideation-index.md:65-67 reports completion in status terms ('Must features at [DEEP] 195/195 — Step 5 complete'), and D-23 (:209) records that the index status cells specifically were 'reconciled deterministically from disk (109 status cells)' — the prose note and the count column were simply not in that reconciliation. No pass decides depth from a descriptive count when the status cell it is printed beside disagrees. Documentation hygiene, no forced invention.

verdicts.claim: 10.01.06's render states and registration lifecycle disagree about whether a credit with no ISRC appears in the list at all.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED on the literal text of both triggers. Empty (:67) fires on 'No **captured credits** on recordings the user played' — not on 'no eligible credits' — so a drummer holding fifteen captured credits is never Empty, and the auditor's implementer-A path requires misreading that cell. Populated (:68) resolves the other half itself: 'One or more eligible credits found | The eligible / registered / collecting list, **each row in its lifecycle state below**' — the pointer is to the whole lifecycle table, which enumerates five states including Blocked (:76) and Conflicted (:78). The named list is shorthand; the normative sentence admits every lifecycle state, which is what makes Blocked renderable at all and is required for the feature's stated purpose ('The gap named upstream', :76; 'money exists, you are not collecting it', :75). Both readings converge on: credits exist → Populated → fifteen Blocked rows.

verdicts.claim: A truncated statement is assigned a state that does not exist in the feature's state machine, and that its sibling explicitly reserves for a different condition it says cannot arise from an incomplete transfer.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED, though the observation is accurate. 10.02.02:124 does assign a truncated file to `Unreadable`, and 10.02.02's States table (:130-145) has no such state — in that file `unreadable` is a row classification (:35). But `Unreadable` is defined, in the sibling: 10.02.01:263 'Unreadable | Ingested; no adapter, or a scanned image | Retained', distinguished from Error at :251. More decisively, the owning feature has a locked decision on this exact scenario: 10.02.01:226 'Network failure mid-upload — truncated file … Intake verifies **file completeness at receipt**, not by inference from the parse. An incomplete transfer is never an ingest (D-15)', restated as D-15 at :331. Pipeline order settles it — 10.02.02's entry state is 'Unparsed | Received from 10.02.01, queued' (:130), so a file intake rejects never reaches the parse, and the state 10.02.02:124 names is unreachable prose rather than a divergent build. Both files also agree on the safety-critical invariant the claim turns on: never `Partial`, never a clean-looking total over partial data, never past the oracle.

verdicts.claim: The sub-domain's Children table reports the pre-deep-dive hypothesis count for all five children, each of which is [DEEP].
verdicts.reason: REFUTED. The facts are right — 10.02-statement-ingestion-normalization-index.md:20-24 each read '`[DEEP]` | 3 hypotheses' while disk carries 17/13/13/10/15 = 68 — but the question the finding says is forced ('whether these nodes have been deep-dived') is answered by the adjacent cell in the same row, which reads `[DEEP]`, and by each file's own header (10.02.01:5 through 10.02.05:5, all '> **Status**: [DEEP]'). Status is the pipeline's depth authority and was the thing deterministically reconciled from disk (ideation-index.md:209, '24 domain index trees reconciled … 109 status cells'); the Deep Think column is descriptive metadata from the 2026-07-16 classification pass that the reconciliation did not touch. Note it is not uniformly stale either: the '3 hypotheses' figure is correct for every [PARTIAL] and [SURFACE] leaf in the domain (10.03.03, 10.03.04, 10.05.02, 10.05.03 all carry exactly 3 on disk), consistent with D-24's '≥2 Deep Think hypotheses each' for Shoulds. Stale bookkeeping beside a correct status cell; no divergence.

verdicts.claim: The sub-domain declares [BREADTH] and three hypotheses per child while two of its four children are [DEEP] with thirteen each.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the [BREADTH] label is prescribed, and the 'identical evidence, two labels' premise is false. ideation-index.md D-23 (:209) states the rule: 'Sub-domains stay `[BREADTH]` (mixed Must-[DEEP]/Should-[SURFACE]) per rollup rule', and D-24 (:210) confirms the end state 'all 24 domains=[BREADTH]'. 10.03 is mixed on disk — 10.03.01 and 10.03.02 [DEEP], 10.03.03 and 10.03.04 [PARTIAL] — so [BREADTH] (10.03-calculation-recoupment-index.md:5) is the correct rollup. The sibling comparison collapses under the same rule: 10.02 is uniformly [DEEP] (all five children Must, all five [DEEP]), so it is not mixed and its [DEEP] label is also correct. Different evidence, different labels, one stated rule. The count column (:20-22, '3 hypotheses' against 13/13/3/3 on disk) is stale for the two [DEEP] rows and correct for the two [PARTIAL] ones, and is descriptive metadata beside a correct per-row status cell.

verdicts.claim: The sub-domain declares [BREADTH] and three hypotheses for 10.05.01 while that file is [DEEP] with twelve.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED for the same reason. 10.05's children are mixed on disk — 10.05.01 [DEEP], 10.05.02 [SURFACE], 10.05.03 [PARTIAL] — so [BREADTH] at 10.05-recovery-leakage-index.md:5 is what ideation-index.md D-23 (:209) prescribes for a mixed sub-domain, not a contradiction of its [DEEP] child. The count discrepancy is real (10.05-recovery-leakage-index.md:20 '3 hypotheses' against 12 DT rows in 10.05.01, and royalties-collections-index.md:36 '9 hypotheses' against 18) but is descriptive metadata printed beside the authoritative status cell, which reads `[DEEP]` in the same row and in the file's own header (10.05.01:5). Nothing forces a pass to re-drill a node whose status cell says [DEEP] and whose global depth completion is recorded at ideation-index.md:65 and :210.
